# P34.41 — withdrawal-barrier bytes: tombstones, alias coverage, entity stubs, /r/<pub>/ landing

**Requirement ids:** none owned (spec §56 names no owner). **Cited
(context, owned elsewhere):** SIG-REL-013 (410 tombstones on every alias
within 15 min — owner **P35.55**), SIG-FIND-001/002 (released discovery /

`docs/tickets/250_P34.41__withdrawal-barrier-bytes.md` (manifest row 250,
Round 11 / P34, sub-round 11A) · **Base:**
`r11/P34.40-serving-topology-dark-v3` (stacked, H2 PR-1) · **Gate:** none
· **Live stage:** none — the bytes go live with the release pipeline

## Why

The withdrawal barrier's deny lines were bare `return 410`s — a withdrawn
route answered nginx's generic error page, not a tombstone, and only the
trailing-slash form of a page route was denied (`/index.html`, the
no-slash form and the `.json` twin fell through to origin bytes — or a
404 that implied removal rather than recorded withdrawal). The
`/entity/<t>/<id>/` convenience stubs pointed at denied bytes,
`page_index` pages kept listing withdrawn records, and `/r/<pub>/` had no
index — a citation visitor at the namespace root got a bare 403. This is
the barrier WV-08's compensating control names for Part VIII and safety
takedowns (C4 NEW-14, NEW-29; G3 §8.3–8.4; ADR-132).

## What ships

- **`exports/src/exports/release.py`** — `apply_withdrawals` now computes
  one deny set split page-vs-file routes and drives everything from it:
  - `_route_targets` yields `(kind, target_id, rel_path, shape)` —
    `page` (directory route: `/<route>`, `/<route>/`,
    `/<route>/index.html` aliases) vs `file` (exact path, e.g. the
    record's `.json` twin, `records.index.jsonl`, `search_index.*`).
  - **Every alias** of a denied route emits a `location =` exact match
    carrying `error_page 410 /conf/tombstone/<sha24>.{html,json}` — the
    410 answers with that route's **own `sig.tombstone/1` body**, staged
    under `conf/tombstone/` (internal-only prefix), never the generic
    nginx page. Conf URI emission fails closed on non-URI-safe routes.
  - `sig.tombstone/1` doc carries `target_kind`, `target_id`,
    `withdrawn_at` (from the recorded disposition's clock),
    public-safe `reason_class`, `disposition_ref` (sha256 over the
    public-safe columns), `superseded_by` (null — the effective
    disposition is current by definition), the release label, and the
    `/corrections/` link — never an e-mail address.
  - **Entity stubs from the deny set:** a `/entity/<t>/<id>/` stub
    denies when its entity is under an entity-level disposition OR the
    ACTIVE release's record route it points at is denied (claim,
    artifact or release deny) — `active_pub` is threaded through
    `activate`/`rollback`/`record_withdrawal`/`release_serving.apply`;
    the stub aliases are covered predictively even before the overlay
    emits the page.
  - **`page_index` coverage:** every staged `page_index.json` is
    scanned; a page embedding a denied entity/claim/artifact id is
    denied whole AND its index entry is marked `withdrawn` +
    `withdrawal_reason` (the "show the tombstone" half — never a
    silently stale listing). Hardlink-safe annotation (ADR-144).
  - A release deny now also globs the `s/<pub>`/`v/<pub>` snapshot
    namespaces and always denies the `r/<pub>` + `releases/<pub>` roots
    — a pre-P34.41 staged tree with no `r/<pub>/index.html` still
    tombstones the namespace root, never 403s.
  - `route_access` normalizes every alias (`/index.html` folds onto the
    page route) and answers the same denial for the `entity/<t>/<id>/`
    stub routes — entity deny, claim deny on the active release's record
    route, or the latest release's namespace deny.
  - Activation/rollback receipts stay JSON-safe: the internal
    route→disposition stub map serialises as its sorted route list.
- **`exports/src/exports/release_pages.py`** — `_layout` gains an
  optional `<meta name="description">`; **`namespace_landing`** renders
  `/r/<pub>/index.html` (namespace orientation: publication id, release
  coordinates, compartment links, manifest/descriptor/landing
  pointers); **`tombstone_page`** carries the full `sig.tombstone/1`
  field set + corrections link; **`entity_stub_tombstone`** renders the
  stub-shaped tombstone. No page embeds an e-mail address.
- **`ops/web/nginx.conf`** — `location /conf/tombstone/ { internal; }`:
  the body files exist only as `error_page 410` internal-redirect
  targets, never directly fetchable.
- **`ops/src/ops/release_serving.py`** — `apply` passes the registry's
  latest pointer as `active_pub` (stubs follow the pointer) and
  serialises the stub map as a sorted route list.
- **`ops/README.md`** — the runbook names the new deny-map shape (every
  alias + per-route tombstone bodies + stub regeneration from the same
  deny set).

## Verification

_Fixture layer (each new behaviour fails if the change is removed):_

- `tests/exports/test_release.py` (+10 tests) — deny map alias
  completeness from the deny set (page triple vs file exact-path, no
  phantom `.json/` aliases); every alias's `error_page` target exists
  and is the route's own tombstone (HTML aliases share the page bytes,
